summary: The MPP charge server's push-mode check verifySacTransfer() fails open: if the RPC result has no envelopeXdr nothing is checked, and the whole check (including verifyFromRawOps, which throws on a wrong amount, asset or recipient) sits in a try/catch whose catch only falls through. Any successful transaction hash, whatever it paid, is accepted as payment.
fix_summary: Throw PaymentVerificationError when envelopeXdr is missing or cannot be parsed, and call verifyFromRawOps outside any catch so a mismatch rejects the credential.

summary: In sponsored (feePayer) mode the server wraps the client-supplied transaction in a fee bump that it signs, with fee = tx.fee * 10 taken from the client's XDR. A paying client sets a huge inner fee and drains the server's fee-payer account.
fix_summary: Cap the fee-bump fee at 10,000,000 stroops (1 XLM), audit item NM-004.
notes: The fix is a per-transaction cap. A report on the fixed commit may still flag the missing cumulative fee budget nearby.

summary: Push-mode ('signature') credentials carry only a transaction hash. The server deduplicates challenge ids but never the hash, so one on-chain payment can be presented against any number of fresh challenges (pay once, claim forever).
fix_summary: Reject a hash already recorded under stellar:tx:{hash}, record it after successful verification, and serialize verify() so get/put cannot race.
notes: The dedup only runs when a store is configured (if (store)); a report on the fixed commit may still flag that replay protection is optional.

summary: When the paid request returns 402 again, the browser paywall decodes fresh PAYMENT-REQUIRED requirements from the server's response and has the wallet sign a new payment for them, so the server can change the amount or recipient on retry or collect a second payment.
fix_summary: Resend the original signed payload on retry and abort if the fresh requirements change scheme, network, asset, payTo or amount.

summary: The x402 middleware guarding paid card creation and funding only compares fields of the client-supplied X-Payment JSON (to, value, txHash present) and then calls next(). The txHash is never checked on-chain or with a facilitator, so a forged header gets a card issued without payment.
fix_summary: Call paymentService.verifyAndAccept() with treasury, asset, amount and network, failing closed (503 if the facilitator is unreachable, 401 if the proof is invalid).

summary: Soroban smart wallet: update_signer() has no require_auth (add_signer, remove_signer and update_contract_code do). Anyone can overwrite an existing signer's public key, limits or storage, taking over the wallet.
fix_summary: Add env.current_contract_address().require_auth() at the top of update_signer.

summary: The sample policy signer, which needs no secret, permits any transfer up to TRANSFER_LIMIT per call and keeps no running total. Repeating capped transfers drains the wallet.
fix_summary: Replace the per-transfer cap with a cumulative 24h rolling allowance stored per wallet (checked_add, TTL renewed, cleared on uninstall).
notes: Sample contract. After the fix the allowance still pays any recipient, by design; a report on the fixed commit may flag that as recipient binding (unauthorized_payment).

summary: Smart account do_check_auth authenticates a Delegated(addr) signer with addr.require_auth_for_args(). The Soroban host approves that without any signature when addr is the direct invoker of this __check_auth, so mutually delegating or self-delegating accounts (or a delegate contract that calls account.require_auth()) are authorized without any key.
fix_summary: Reject a Delegated signer whose address is the contract of any authorized context (validate_no_delegated_context_contract, error 3017) and refuse self-delegated signers at configuration time.

summary: collect_fee with Eager approval approves max_fee_amount for the forwarder but pulls only fee_amount. The unspent allowance survives into the arbitrary target invocation and later forwards, where it can be drained from the user.
fix_summary: In Eager mode pull the whole max_fee_amount, pay the fee and return the remainder to the user, so no allowance survives the collection.
notes: Lazy mode still leaves an allowance, by design and documented; do not count a Lazy-mode finding against the fixed commit.

summary: Payment-channel factory open() and the channel constructor/top_up require the funder's auth only when amount > 0. Anyone can open a zero-deposit channel naming any funder, with an attacker-chosen commitment key and recipient, at the deterministic address derived from (from, salt). Funds the victim later sends to that address can then be closed out by the attacker.
fix_summary: Always call from.require_auth() in factory open and in top_up (the transfer is skipped when the amount is zero).

summary: The SEP-7 parser accepts query parameters after 'signature', but signature verification cuts the payload at '&signature='. A validly signed pay URI with '&amount=5000&memo=...' appended still verifies against the origin domain, while the wallet acts on the appended amount and memo.
fix_summary: Refuse any parameter after signature (and a percent-encoded signature name) in the parser, and make verification refuse the same shapes through signed_prefix().

summary: The transaction submission service reconciles a submitted payment only by its outer fee-bump hash and treats a Horizon 404 as 'did not land', then rebuilds and resubmits. Anyone can re-wrap SDP's signed inner payment in a new fee bump (CAP-15), so the payment lands under another hash and SDP pays the receiver again.
fix_summary: On a 404 for the outer hash, look up the inner transaction hash derived from xdr_sent; only a 404 on both means it did not land. Record the hash that actually landed.

summary: Payments are built with Amount.StringFixed(6), rounding Stellar's 7-decimal amounts, so the amount signed differs from the amount approved (upstream the dispatcher also round-trips amounts through float64).
fix_summary: Use StringFixed(7) when building the payment; the dispatcher parses amounts with decimal.NewFromString and rejects amounts with more than 7 decimals.

summary: SEP-10 challenge validation for existing accounts only requires the summed weight of matching signatures to reach the account's medium threshold. For a default account that is 0 < 0, so a challenge with no client signature authenticates as that account, and the server's own signature is never excluded.
fix_summary: Attribute every signature to exactly one expected signer, require at least one client signer, exclude the server signing key and reject unmatched or duplicate signatures.

summary: The sponsored-transaction builder signs, with the tenant's distribution account as source and fee payer, a user-supplied InvokeHostFunction whose auth entries may come from any contract (contract, claimable-balance and liquidity-pool cases fall through). A user names a contract they control as authorizer, runs their own __check_auth under sponsorship and drives the resource fee to the network maximum, draining the tenant's fee reserve.
fix_summary: Require every auth entry to come from the caller's own embedded-wallet contract (ValidateAuthEntriesFromContract), enforced in the HTTP handler and again in the transaction submission service before signing.
notes: The validator called at the fixed location lives in internal/utils, outside the audited subdir.

summary: check_trustlines marks every pending_trust deposit pending_execution_attempt=True, then never resets it when the account fails to load, when the trustline is not there yet, or for the remaining transactions after one submit() raises (it returns). Those deposits are never picked up again and stay stuck.
fix_summary: Reset pending_execution_attempt on every exit path (failed account load, no trustline, multisig, submit error) and break instead of return.
notes: No funds are lost (deposits stall). Same commit fixes similar paths in execute_outgoing_transactions.py and poll_pending_deposits.py.
